arxiv-2007-05685.title: NeuralExplorer: State Space Exploration of Closed Loop Control Systems Using Neural Networks
arxiv-2007-05685.creator: Manish Goyal, Parasara Sridhar Duggirala, {manishg,psd}@cs.unc.edu
arxiv-2007-05685.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a framework for performing state space exploration of closed loop control systems. Our approach involves approximating sensitivity and a newly introduced notion of inverse sensitivity by a neural network. We show how the approximation of sensitivity and inverse sensitivity can be used for computing estimates of the reachable set.

arxiv-2101-11517.title: Investigating Bi-Level Optimization for Learning and Vision from a Unified Perspective: A Survey and Beyond
arxiv-2101-11517.creator: Risheng Liu, Jiaxin Gao, Jin Zhang, Deyu Meng, and Zhouchen Lin
arxiv-2101-11517.description: Abstract Bi-Level Optimization (BLO) is originated from the area of economic game theory and then introduced into the optimization community. BLO is able to handle problems with a hierarchical structure, involving two levels of optimization tasks, where one task is nested inside the other.

arxiv-2112-06070.title: A Comparative Study on Robust Graph Neural Networks to Structural Noises
arxiv-2112-06070.creator: Zeyu Zhang, Yulong Pei
arxiv-2112-06070.description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) learn node representations by passing and aggregating messages between neighboring nodes. GNNs have been applied successfully in several application domains and achieved promising performance. However, GNNs could be vulnerable to structural noise because of the message passing mechanism where noise may be propagated through the entire graph.

arxiv-2204-03897.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Compliant Bipedal Locomotion on Torque Sensor-Less Gear-Driven Humanoid
arxiv-2204-03897.creator: Shimpei Masuda, Kuniyuki Takahashi
arxiv-2204-03897.description: Abstract Sim-to-real is a mainstream method to cope with the large number of trials needed by typical deep reinforcement learning methods. However, transferring a policy trained in simulation to actual hardware remains an open challenge due to the reality gap . In particular, the characteristics of actuators in legged robots have a considerable influence on sim-to-real transfer.

arxiv-2205-04354.title: Role of liquid driving on the clogging of constricted particle suspensions
arxiv-2205-04354.creator: Mathieu Souzy, Alvaro Marin
arxiv-2205-04354.description: Abstract Forcing dense suspensions of non-cohesive particles through constrictions might either result in a continuous flow, an intermittent one, or indefinite interruption of flow, i.e., a clog. While one of the most important (and obvious) controlling parameters in such a system is the neck-to-particle size ratio, the role of the liquid driving method is not so obvious.

arxiv-2305-19256.title: Ambient Diffusion: Learning Clean Distributions from Corrupted Data
arxiv-2305-19256.creator: Giannis Daras UT Austin giannisdaras@utexas.edu Kulin Shah UT Austin kulinshah@utexas.edu Yuval Dagan UC Berkeley yuvald@berkeley.edu Aravind Gollakota UT Austin aravindg@cs.utexas.edu Alexandros G. Dimakis UT Austin dimakis@austin.utexas.edu Adam Klivans UT Austin klivans@utexas.edu
arxiv-2305-19256.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Giannis Daras UT Austin giannisdaras@utexas.edu Kulin Shah UT Austin kulinshah@utexas.edu Yuval Dagan UC Berkeley yuvald@berkeley.edu Aravind Gollakota UT Austin aravindg@cs.utexas.edu Alexandros G. Dimakis UT Austin dimakis@austin.utexas.edu Adam Klivans UT Austin klivans@utexas.edu. We present the first diffusion-based framework that can learn an unknown distribution using only highly-corrupted samples. This problem arises in scientific applications where access to uncorrupted samples is impossible or expensive to acquire.

arxiv-2307-10752.title: On competing ( p , q ) − \left(p,q\right)- Laplacian Drichlet problem with unbounded weight
arxiv-2307-10752.creator: Josef Diblik, Marek Galewski, Igor Kossowski, Dumitru Motreanu
arxiv-2307-10752.description: Abstract We investigate the existence of generalized solutions to coercive competing system driven by the ( p , q ) − \left(p,q\right)- Laplacian with unbounded perturbation corresponding to the leading term in the differential operator and with convection depending on the gradient. Some abstract principle leading to the existence of generalized solutions is also derived basing on the Galerkin scheme.

arxiv-2311-03807.title: Twisted categorical generic fiber
arxiv-2311-03807.creator: Hayato Morimura
arxiv-2311-03807.description: Abstract . After extending Orlov’s theorem, we prove specialization of derived equivalence for flat proper families of Azumaya varieties. 1. arxiv-2403-16898.title: Concerned with Data Contamination? Assessing Countermeasures in Code Language Model
arxiv-2403-16898.creator: Jialun Cao, Wuqi Zhang, Shing-Chi Cheung
arxiv-2403-16898.description: Abstract Various techniques have been proposed to leverage the capabilities of code language models (CLMs) for software engineering tasks. While these techniques typically evaluate their effectiveness using publicly available datasets, the evaluation can be subject to data contamination threats where the evaluation datasets have already been used to train the concerned CLMs.

arxiv-2406-12644.title: Hierarchical Prompting Taxonomy: A Universal Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models Aligned with Human Cognitive Principles
arxiv-2406-12644.creator: Devichand Budagam, Ashutosh Kumar, Mahsa Khoshnoodi, Sankalp KJ, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha
arxiv-2406-12644.description: Abstract . Assessing the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in performing different tasks is crucial for understanding their strengths and weaknesses. This paper presents Hierarchical Prompting Taxonomy (HPT), grounded on human cognitive principles and designed to assess LLMs by examining the cognitive demands of various tasks.

arxiv-2407-18838.title: The Role of Temporal Hierarchy in Spiking Neural Networks
arxiv-2407-18838.creator: Filippo Moro, Pau Vilimelis Aceituno, Laura Kriener, Melika Payvand
arxiv-2407-18838.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Filippo Moro, Pau Vilimelis Aceituno, Laura Kriener, Melika Payvand. SNN have the potential for rich spatio-temporal signal processing thanks to exploiting both spatial and temporal parameters. The temporal dynamics such as time constants of the synapses and neurons and delays have been recently shown to have computational benefits that help reduce the overall number of parameters required in the network and increase the accuracy of the SNN in solving temporal tasks.

arxiv-2412-14366.title: Surrealistic-like Image Generation with Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2412-14366.creator: Elif Ayten, Shuai Wang, Hjalmar Snoep
arxiv-2412-14366.description: Abstract Recent advances in generative AI make it convenient to create different types of content, including text, images, and code. In this paper, we explore the generation of images in the style of paintings in the surrealism movement using vision-language generative models, including DALL-E, Deep Dream Generator, and DreamStudio.

arxiv-2501-00731.title: Polarized electron bunch refresh rates in an electron storage ring
arxiv-2501-00731.creator: S. R. Mane
arxiv-2501-00731.description: Abstract When polarized electron bunches are injected and circulated in a high-energy storage ring, the polarization of the bunches relaxes to the asymptotic value of the radiative polarization, caused by the synchrotron radiation. Hence the bunches must be refreshed periodically, to maintain a predetermined time-averaged value of the bunch polarization.

arxiv-2501-05457.title: The Jungle of Generative Drug Discovery: Traps, Treasures, and Ways Out
arxiv-2501-05457.creator: Rıza Özçelik, Francesca Grisoni*
arxiv-2501-05457.description: Abstract “How to evaluate de novo designs proposed by a generative model?” Despite the transformative potential of generative deep learning in drug discovery, this seemingly simple question has no clear answer. The absence of standardized guidelines challenges both the benchmarking of generative approaches and the selection of molecules for prospective studies.

arxiv-2503-16565.title: Gene42 : Long-Range Genomic Foundation Model With Dense Attention
arxiv-2503-16565.creator: Kirill Vishniakov, Boulbaba Ben Amor †, Engin Tekin, Nancy A. ElNaker, Karthik Viswanathan, Aleksandr Medvedev, Aahan Singh, Maryam Nadeem, Mohammad Amaan Sayeed, Praveenkumar Kanithi, Tiago Magalhaes, Natalia Vassilieva, Dwarikanath Mahapatra, Marco Pimentel, Shadab Khan
arxiv-2503-16565.description: Abstract We introduce Gene42, a novel family of Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs) designed to manage context lengths of up to 192,000 base pairs (bp) at a single-nucleotide resolution. Gene42 models utilize a decoder-only (LLaMA-style) architecture with a dense self-attention mechanism.

arxiv-2509-20566.title: Nonlocal Magic Generation and Information Scrambling in Noisy Clifford Circuits
arxiv-2509-20566.creator: Emanuel Dallas, Paolo Zanardi
arxiv-2509-20566.description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the average information scrambling and nonlocal magic generation properties of random Clifford encoding-decoding circuits perturbed by local noise. We quantify these with the bipartite algebraic out-of-time order correlator ( 𝒜 \mathcal{A} -OTOC) and average Pauli-entangling power (APEP) respectively.

europmc-pmc3323154.creator: Miller MW, Williams ES, Hobbs NT, Wolfe LL.
europmc-pmc3323154.description: Whether transmission of the chronic wasting disease (CWD) prion among cervids requires direct interaction with infected animals has been unclear. pmc-11460008.title: Implementation of the four habits model in intermediate care services in Norway: a process evaluation
pmc-11460008.creator: Linda Aimée Hartford Kvæl, Pål Gulbrandsen, Anne Werner, Astrid Bergland
pmc-11460008.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundIntermediate care (IC) services bridge the transition for older patients from the hospital to the home. Despite the goal of involving individuals in their recovery process, these services often become standardised, leading to communication breakdowns. While evidence-based practices, such as the Four Habits Model (4HM), for effective communication are crucial for enhancing high-quality healthcare, research suggests their integration into routine practice remains limited.

pmc-11642226.title: Blood-Based Clinical Biomarkers of Inflammation and Nutrition in Hyperemesis Gravidarum
pmc-11642226.creator: Busra Demir Cendek, Burak Bayraktar, Zeynep Seyhanli, Ezgi Kocyildiz, Hakan Golbasi, Mujde Can Ibanoglu, Yaprak Engin Ustun, C Andrew Combs
pmc-11642226.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: In this study, the aim was to investigate blood-based clinical biomarkers of inflammation and nutrition indices in hyperemesis gravidarum (HG). Methods: This retrospective case–control study was conducted at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2022. A total of 820 pregnant women were enrolled in this study; 410 pregnant women were diagnosed with HG (HG group) at 6–14 weeks of gestation, and 410 pregnant women were healthy controls (control group) in the same gestational weeks.

pmc-13374514.title: RNA•DNA:DNA triplex formation by HIF1α-AS1 modulates individual base pair stabilities in the adrenomedullin DNA target duplex
pmc-13374514.creator: Nina M. Krause, Julia Wirmer-Bartoschek, Christian Richter, Matthias S. Leisegang, Ralf P. Brandes, Harald Schwalbe
pmc-13374514.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) play key roles in gene regulation. One potential regulation mechanism involves the formation of RNA•DNA:DNA triplexes. In these triplexes, the lncRNA binds in the major groove of a target DNA via Hoogsteen base pair formation. Here, we investigated the impact of the underlying RNA binding on the stability of the DNA duplex target to gain insights into the triplex stability at base pair resolution with an isolated triplex system.
